def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Returns priority with which we want to add item to each bin.
    Args:
        item: Size of item to be added to the bin.
        bins: Array of capacities for each bin.
    Return:
        Array of same size as bins with priority score of each bin.
    """
    remaining = bins - item
    priorities = np.full_like(bins, -np.inf)
    
    # Ideal underfit: leaves between 0 and 0.3*item remaining (highest priority)
    ideal_under_mask = (remaining > 0) & (remaining <= 0.3 * item)
    priorities[ideal_under_mask] = 3 - remaining[ideal_under_mask]
    
    # Exact fit: second highest priority
    exact_mask = remaining == 0
    priorities[exact_mask] = 2
    
    # Moderate underfit: leaves more than 0.3*item remaining
    moderate_under_mask = remaining > 0.3 * item
    priorities[moderate_under_mask] = 1 - remaining[moderate_under_mask] / item
    
    # Tolerable overfit: consumes up to 1.5*item total (negative remaining > -0.5*item)
    tolerable_over_mask = (remaining < 0) & (remaining > -0.5 * item)
    priorities[tolerable_over_mask] = -1 - np.abs(remaining[tolerable_over_mask]) / item
    
    return priorities

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    remaining = bins - item
    priorities = np.full_like(bins, -np.inf)
    valid_mask = remaining >= 0
    if np.any(valid_mask):
        remaining_valid = remaining[valid_mask]
        bins_valid = bins[valid_mask]
        ratio = remaining_valid / bins_valid
        target_ratio = 0.1
        priorities[valid_mask] = 1.0 - np.abs(ratio - target_ratio) - 0.5 * (item / bins_valid)
    return priorities

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Returns priority with which we want to add item to each bin.
    Args:
        item: Size of item to be added to the bin.
        bins: Array of capacities for each bin.
    Return:
        Array of same size as bins with priority score of each bin.
    """
    remaining = bins - item
    # Avoid negative remaining capacities (invalid bins)
    valid_mask = remaining >= 0
    priorities = np.full_like(bins, -np.inf)
    
    # Compute relative utilization: ratio of item size to remaining capacity
    # Use a smooth function that peaks when item is around half of remaining capacity
    relative_util = np.where(valid_mask, item / remaining, np.inf)
    
    # Reward bins where item is approximately half of remaining capacity
    # This creates a peak at relative_util ≈ 2 (i.e., item ≈ 0.5 * remaining)
    # We use a Gaussian-like shape centered at 2
    deviations = np.abs(relative_util - 2.0)
    priorities[valid_mask] = -deviations
    
    return priorities
